subject: Walkland Court Redevelopment and McGlynn Playground Funding
overview: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed several high-value funding applications for open space, historic preservation, and affordable housing projects. Significant discussion focused on the multi-million dollar requests for the Walkland Court housing redevelopment and the McGlynn school playground reconstruction.

items.title: Carr Park Pickleball Courts
items.summary: The committee reviewed a $402,000 request for four dedicated pickleball courts, addressing concerns regarding tree root protection, safety fencing near baseball fields, and the loss of green space to pavement.

items.title: Gillis Park Picnic and Fitness Area
items.summary: Proponents presented a $92,000 proposal for a picnic area and adult fitness area intended to expand the user base at the baseball field as part of a larger ADA accessibility project.

items.title: COVID-19 Memorial Grove
items.summary: The committee discussed a $28,000 request for design services and public outreach to identify a location for a contemplative grove commemorating pandemic victims.

items.title: McGlynn University Accessible Playground
items.summary: Proponents requested $900,000 in CPA funds toward a $2.6 million universally accessible playground, though the committee requested more detailed budget and maintenance information before deliberation.

items.title: Isaac Hall House Exterior Restoration
items.summary: The committee considered an $85,000 application for historic window restoration at the Paul Revere's first stop site, noting that a preservation restriction would be a condition of public funding for the private property.

items.title: Shiloh Baptist Church Window Restoration
items.summary: Representatives requested $150,000 to restore historic stained-glass windows, and the committee recommended pursuing state register listing to qualify for broader grant opportunities.

items.title: Walkland Court Affordable Housing Redevelopment
items.summary: The Medford Housing Authority presented a multi-year $2.4 million request for a deeply affordable housing expansion, with discussion centered on funding caps for pre-development costs and the potential for bonding construction funds.

items.title: Administrative Business and Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from September 13, 2022, and adjourned.
